title: Templates: Testing and Design Practice
learningObjectives: Explain templates: testing and design practice.
Identify template parameters and required operations.
Design a reusable generic utility or type.

understand.concept: Generic code should be tested across several supported types, edge cases and constraints. Avoid hidden assumptions such as copying, arithmetic, ordering or default construction unless required.
understand.whyItMatters: Multiple instantiations reveal type-specific errors and overly narrow assumptions.
understand.explain: Write the supported-type contract, compile/test several instantiations, and include negative tests for types that should not be accepted.

examples.title: Test types
examples.code: template<class T>T square(T v){return v*v;}\nint a=square(3);double b=square(2.5);

examples.title: Boundary cases
examples.code: template<class T>T twice(T v){return v+v;}\n// test 0 and positive/negative where supported
examples.explanation: Boundary values help verify generic behavior.

examples.title: Unsupported operation
examples.code: template<class T>auto combine(T a,T b){return a+b;}\n// type without + cannot instantiate
examples.explanation: Requirements must be documented or constrained.

examples.title: Avoid copy requirement
examples.explanation: Const-reference form can accept non-copyable objects.

practise.guidedTask: Analyze each Templates: Testing and Design Practice example: identify parameters, requirements, deduced or explicit arguments, and instantiated behavior.
practise.independentTask: Write a generic C++ utility or type demonstrating templates: testing and design practice. Test two supported types, one boundary case, and one unsupported/constrained type; explain why it is or is not accepted.
hints: Begin with a concrete example before generalizing.
Name template parameters for their roles.

options: Instantiation when required operation is invalid
